text:
maya: quick note — during the cert rotation in eu-west at ~20:18 UTC we hit a routing / DNS propagation issue. traffic landed on stale edge IPs, LB marked pool down, and we saw GPU pod churn. starting a post-incident runbook pass.

ali: saw a spike of 502/504s and reconnect storms. kube events show nodes drained and pods restarted; not a pure OOM. dns lookup traces show old A records cached for ~6m despite TTL being 60s.

frank: confirmed — cloud-dns accepted the update instantly but upstream caches (internal infra and some edge proxies) kept old entries. when proxies lost backend health we kicked drain logic which made things worse.

linda: automated weighted-shift to other regions happened (good) but it created a lot of fanout retries. costs spiked and tail latency increased. had to revert weights manually after stabilization.

ops-bot: Incident INC-2026-0453 created: eu-west routing anomaly during cert rotation. tags: dns,gpu,failover,runbook.

katie: short summary: certificate rotation -> DNS update -> propagation lag -> LB health flips -> node drain -> pod churn -> retries -> increased cost and latency.

maya: initial RCA hypothesis: we rotate certs which changes endpoint metadata -> update pushes to cloud-dns -> some internal resolvers/proxies don't respect low TTLs, so clients keep hitting old IPs until caches expire -> health probes fail -> control-plane starts draining pods (node/pool-level drain policy) before new registrations stabilized.

ali: mitigation timeline:
- 20:18 detect 5xx spike
- 20:20 automated weighted-shift to other regions kicks in
- 20:24 manual override of weights, reduce cross-region blast
- 20:29 rollback immediate cert metadata change for affected edge pool
- 20:36 stable; decrease retries and re-routed traffic back gradually

frank: logs/samples attached (trimmed):
```
# dns lookup traces from edge-proxy
;; ANSWER SECTION:
edge.redwood-eu 60 IN A 34.12.22.10
# later still returning old ip from cache until 6m mark
```

linda: propose runbook updates (draft):
- add DNS propagation preflight: run `dig +trace` and synthetic curl from multiple internal regions and public vantage points (us-west, ap-southeast, eu-west) and only proceed if >90% show new IP within 90s.
- add a soft-drain policy for node drains during rollout: require 2 separate successful LB health check registrations from new pods before marking capacity decreased.
- add fallback: instead of immediate cross-region weighted-shift, keep short circuit to local cold pool with circuit breaker to avoid fanout of retries.
- instrument cost alarms to trigger when cross-region bandwidth > X for 5m.

maya: specific checks to add to runbook (commands):
```
# quick DNS preflight
for r in {us-west,eu-west,ap-southeast}; do dig +short edge.redwood-${r} || true; done
# vantage curl
curl -sS -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n" https://edge.redwood-eu/health || true
# k8s: ensure new pods registered with LB
kubectl get endpoints -n infra edge-proxy | grep <new-ip>
```

katie: also recommend changing our DNS TTLs strategy. for planned rollouts, set a lower TTL (30s) 10m before the change, but ensure internal resolvers will honor it. add a validation: query at least 3 internal resolver IPs and 2 public ones.

ali: add synthetic check endpoints on edge-proxy that include the pod id in the response so we can detect which pods are serving. runbook should require verifying that new pod ids appear in health queries before any node drain completes.

oncall-sre: action items (owners + dates):
- maya: draft PR for runbook changes (dns preflight + soft-drain) — due 2026-03-25
- ali: create synthetic multi-vantagepoint checker script and deploy to runbook tools — due 2026-03-22
- frank: add pod-id health endpoint + LB registration check into edge-proxy — due 2026-03-29
- linda: update weighted-shift policy to include circuit-breaker and cost guardrails — due 2026-03-28
- katie: run DNS TTL behavior matrix across cloud providers and internal resolvers, document quirks — due 2026-03-30

maya: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runbooks/pull/279 — contains the proposed soft-drain policy and preflight checklist. please review.

frank: +1 to the soft-drain. also adding a risk note: if LB health checks are flaky, soft-drain could delay critical rollbacks. need an override path and clear SLA for rollback.

linda: agreed. runbook will include an override flag `--force-drain` for emergency rollbacks with an approval step (pager+ack).

katie: postmortem doc draft will include cost delta: +18% infra egress/cold-start during the failover window. will attach to INC-2026-0453.

maya: follow-up: update deploy checklist to include a mandatory post-rotation monitoring window and a go/no-go gate based on synthetic checks.

ali: I'll add monitoring dashboards: DNS divergence rate, LB health flips by region, cross-region bandwidth by service, and pod-id registration latency.

ops-bot: Incident INC-2026-0453 status: stabilized -> postmortem in progress -> owners assigned.

maya: thanks team. final note: treat DNS as first-class for planned infra changes. low TTLs alone are not sufficient; we need multi-vantage validation + conservative drain semantics. closing thread after runbook PR merged and synthetic checker live. :thumbsup:
